# RunStrict

> Last updated: 2026-09-11. 40-day seasons roll over automatically; the current season number and its dates are shown live at https://runstrict.com. 1,200+ active runners across 8 cities. Scoring rules v2 (per-team point tables, no multipliers) are described below.

> RunStrict is a free GPS running game for iOS, Android, Apple Watch, and Wear OS where runners physically capture hexagonal territory tiles by running through them. Players choose one of three teams — FLAME, WAVE, or CHAOS — at season registration and compete to control their city's map before a 40-day season resets the scoreboard in an event called The Void. The site is available in 11 languages.

## What is RunStrict?

RunStrict is a location-based running app that gamifies outdoor running. Using GPS tracking and Uber's H3 hexagonal grid system (resolution 9, ~175m per hex), every step a runner takes flips territory on a real city map to their team's color. The last runner through a hex owns it. It is sometimes described as "Strava meets Risk" or a "Pokémon GO for runners," but it requires real running with pace verification.

## Key Features

- **GPS Territory Capture**: Run through ~175m hexagonal tiles to flip them to your team's color in real-time
- **Three Teams**: FLAME (Red), WAVE (Blue), CHAOS (Purple) — all three chosen at season registration, locked for the season, each with its own scoring table (see Teams)
- **Three Kinds of Hex**: every hex you cross is new ground (never run by anyone, in any season), a friendly hex (your team already holds it) or an enemy hex. Each team splits the same 10 points across the three — no multipliers, no buffs
- **Territory Ladder**: hexes roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents; region labels show the leading home province, continent markers show the leading nationality's flag
- **40-Day Seasons**: Every season ends with "The Void" — points, rankings and team picks reset. The hex map persists across seasons ("the land remembers")
- **Anti-Cheat**: 25 km/h speed cap, accelerometer verification, GPS accuracy ≤50m required, under 12 min/km pace (20 s moving average) to capture
- **Battery Optimized**: 0.5 Hz GPS polling, no WebSocket, syncs only on launch/resume/run completion
- **Tiered Leaderboards**: Province, District, and Zone scope rankings
- **Privacy First**: No runner IDs stored in hex data; ownership is only ever shown as team color, province name or nation flag — never per person
- **Pace Consistency Score**: CV-based stability metric rewards steady runners
- **Wearables**: Apple Watch and Wear OS companion apps with wrist-first run controls, live pace, and hex-capture alerts

## Platform Availability

- **iOS**: Available now on the App Store (iOS 15+) — https://apps.apple.com/us/app/runstrict/id6760189457
- **Android**: Available now on Google Play (Android 10+) — https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.neondialactic.runstrict
- **Apple Watch**: Available now (watchOS 10+) — companion bundled with the iPhone app
- **Wear OS**: Available now (Wear OS 3+ / SDK 30; Galaxy Watch 4+, Pixel Watch) — companion via Google Play. Tile, complication, and wrist-first run controls; runs survive a dropped phone connection
- **Languages**: The website is localized in 11 languages — English, Korean, Japanese, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Arabic, and Hindi

## How It Works

1. Open RunStrict and start running — GPS tracks your route in real-time
2. Keep your pace under 12 min/km (20-second moving average) to activate hex capture mode
3. Every ~175m hex tile you run through flips to your team's color
4. The last runner through a hex holds it — speed and consistency matter
5. Each hex is scored as new / friendly / enemy using your team's point table (see Teams); the server classifies and scores every run against the previous midnight's map snapshot
6. Compete on tiered leaderboards (Zone, District, Province); zoom out to see which home province holds each region and which nationality holds each continent
7. When the 40-day season ends, The Void wipes points, ranks and team picks; the map persists, and a new season begins automatically

## Teams

Every team splits the same **10 points** across three kinds of hex. The split is the team's doctrine.

| Team | Doctrine | New ground | Friendly hex | Enemy hex |
|------|----------|-----------:|-------------:|----------:|
| FLAME (Red) | Attack | 3 | 1 | **6** |
| WAVE (Blue) | Hold | 3 | **6** | 1 |
| CHAOS (Purple) | Explore | **6** | 2 | 2 |

- **New ground** = a hex nobody has ever run, in any season. Because the map persists between seasons, new ground only gets rarer.
- **Friendly hex** = a hex your team already holds (as of the previous midnight's snapshot). Pays **once per hex per day**.
- **Enemy hex** = a hex held by another team. Pays every run.
- Team choice happens once, at season registration, for all three teams. It is locked until The Void. There is no mid-season defection ("Traitor's Gate" was removed).
- The table is the whole scoring rule: there are no buff multipliers, Elite/Common tiers, turnout or participation bonuses. Values are served from the server config so they can be tuned without an app update.

### FLAME (Red) — attack
Built to take ground. An enemy hex is worth 6 points — the biggest single score in the game — while friendly hexes pay only 1. Best for runners who push into the other side's streets.

### WAVE (Blue) — hold
Built to hold ground. Re-running a hex your team already holds pays 6 (once per hex per day), so WAVE wins by showing up every day on the same streets, together.

### CHAOS (Purple) — explore
Built to go where no one has run. A hex nobody has ever touched is worth 6; everything else pays 2. Best for runners who map out untouched streets.

## Territory Ownership

- Levels: hex (H3 res 9) → province (res 5) → country (res 4) → region (res 3) → continent (res 1).
- Team color (last runner's team) always decides who holds a hex; province/country/continent team dominance is settled nightly.
- In parallel, a nightly batch (midnight GMT+2) rolls up two owner dimensions from the map snapshot: the runners' **registered home province** and their **nationality**. Region zoom labels each region with the leading home province name (e.g. "Seoul 2"); continent zoom shows the flag of the leading nationality.
- Ties keep the previous day's owner; if there was none, the level is unowned.
- Per-hex owner attributes are stored for aggregation only and are never exposed per hex.

## Technology

- **Hex Grid**: Uber's H3 geospatial indexing at resolution 9 (~175m hexes); districts at resolution 6, provinces at resolution 5, countries at resolution 4, regions at resolution 3, continents at resolution 1
- **Backend**: Supabase (PostgreSQL + RLS + Edge Functions); serverless, no custom API server
- **Client**: Flutter (iOS, Android, Wear OS) and a native Apple Watch companion
- **Timezone**: Game logic uses GMT+2; seasons roll over at midnight GMT+2

## Comparisons

RunStrict differs from traditional running apps (Strava, Nike Run Club, Runkeeper) by adding a competitive territory-capture game layer. Unlike fitness trackers that focus on personal metrics, RunStrict makes every run a strategic move in a team game. It also differs from location games like Pokémon GO by requiring actual physical running (with pace verification) rather than walking.

## FAQ

**Is RunStrict free?**
Yes, completely free to download and play, on both iOS and Android.

**What devices does it support?**
iPhone (iOS 15+), Android (10+), Apple Watch (watchOS 10+), and Wear OS (3+ / SDK 30 — Galaxy Watch 4+, Pixel Watch). All companion apps are available now.

**How are points scored?**
Each hex you cross is new ground, a friendly hex or an enemy hex, and your team's table sets the points: FLAME 3 / 1 / 6, WAVE 3 / 6 / 1, CHAOS 6 / 2 / 2 (new / friendly / enemy). Friendly hexes pay once per hex per day. There are no multipliers or buffs.

**Can I cheat with GPS spoofing?**
No. RunStrict uses accelerometer verification, a 25 km/h speed cap, and GPS accuracy requirements to prevent spoofing.

**What happens when a season ends?**
The Void resets season points, rankings and team assignments. The hex map persists — the land remembers its last runner's team color — and a snapshot of the final map is archived. A new 40-day season begins automatically and everyone picks a team again.

**Can I switch teams?**
Not during a season. You choose FLAME, WAVE or CHAOS at registration and the choice is locked until The Void. Every new season starts with a fresh choice among all three.

**What counts as "new ground"?**
A hex that nobody has ever run, in any season. Once anyone has run it, it is either friendly or enemy from then on.

**Does it drain battery?**
No. RunStrict uses 0.5 Hz GPS polling (once every 2 seconds) and syncs data only on app launch, resume, and run completion — no persistent connections.

**How big are the hexes?**
Each hex is approximately 175 meters edge-to-edge, using Uber's H3 resolution 9 grid system.

**Where is RunStrict available?**
Globally — territory capture works in any city with GPS coverage. The app is on the App Store and Google Play worldwide, and the website is localized in 11 languages.
